summary: Flat-file Markdown wiki graph linter. Use when `quality` needs to ask whether the docs form a CONNECTED graph — orphan pages, disconnected islands, largest-component ratio — a question `check_doc_links.py` does not ask, because it validates whether each link RESOLVES, not whether a page is reachable at all.

commands: if command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1; then cargo install --git https://github.com/corca-ai/awiki --rev f65f8c43dbf0300609bdfdf823c09cba370222c6 --locked awiki; elif command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1; then brew install corca-ai/tap/awiki; else curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/corca-ai/awiki/releases/latest/download/awiki-installer.sh | sh; fi
notes: The cargo path is FIRST because it is the only one that pins: upstream tag `v0.5.0` at immutable revision `f65f8c43dbf0300609bdfdf823c09cba370222c6`. The revision is what the install resolves; the tag is carried beside it because a tag can move and a revision cannot. `--locked` is load-bearing — it honours the upstream lockfile so the build does not silently resolve newer transitive dependencies than the pinned revision was verified against.

There is no crates.io release, so cargo must install from the git repository. Upstream DOES publish release binaries: v0.5.0 ships `awiki-installer.sh`, a Homebrew formula (`awiki.rb`), and prebuilt tarballs for linux and darwin on both x86_64 and aarch64. A machine without a Rust toolchain can therefore still install awiki, and must not be told to degrade instead.

The brew and installer-script fallbacks resolve the LATEST RELEASE, not the pinned revision — they trade reproducibility for not needing a toolchain. Use the cargo path when the exact captured version matters.
No release asset targets Windows; the cargo path is the only one that serves it, and it needs a Rust toolchain.
After installation, ensure the install bin directory is on PATH and verify with `awiki --version` before trusting any docs-graph output.

The install pins an exact revision, so an update is a deliberate re-pin, not a refresh: change the `--rev` in this manifest and re-run the install command. `cargo install --git` without a new revision reinstalls the SAME commit.

A version bump re-opens the parse contract. `awiki lint` output is consumed by parsing its `// lint_failed documents=... orphans=...` summary line, which is not a declared stable interface — re-capture the quality fixture and re-read the summary format before promoting a new version.

detect.failure_hint: Install `awiki` before running the docs-graph observation; do not report `check_doc_links.py` link validity as if it answered the orphan/island question.

healthcheck.failure_hint: The `awiki` binary exists but its help surface is not healthy. Reinstall at the pinned revision, then rerun the docs-graph observation.

version_expectation.constraint: Prefer 0.5.0, the version this repo's captured docs-graph fixture was taken at (upstream tag v0.5.0, revision f65f8c43dbf0300609bdfdf823c09cba370222c6).

notes: Installed from the upstream git repository, not from crates.io: `cargo install --git https://github.com/corca-ai/awiki --rev <revision> --locked awiki`.
`--locked` is load-bearing — it honours the upstream lockfile so the build does not silently resolve newer transitive dependencies than the pinned revision was verified against.

when_missing: The docs-graph question cannot be answered without `awiki`; report it as not-run rather than substituting `check_doc_links.py`, whose semantics are distinct — it checks that a link RESOLVES, not that a page is REACHABLE — or `markdownlint`, which is a style linter and answers neither. The measured split is in `<authoring-repo>/docs/docs-graph-checks.md`.

Do not report a clean docs verdict on the strength of the other markdown gates passing: orphan and island counts are unobserved when this binary is absent, and unobserved is not zero. The `docs-graph` quality lane enforces this itself by exiting UNESTABLISHED rather than 0.
when_version_mismatch: NO AUTOMATED DETECTOR EXISTS for this condition, and this text is agent-facing guidance rather than something a gate enforces. `version_expectation.policy` is `advisory`, so `control_plane_lib` records `observed_version` without comparing it to anything, and `check_quality_tool_fixtures.py` deliberately never re-runs the tool. Read the installed version from `doctor.version.observed_version` in the generated `integrations/locks/awiki.json` and compare it yourself against the `version` field of `charness-artifacts/quality/fixtures/awiki-0.5.0-docs-lint.json`.

The `awiki lint` summary line (`// lint_failed documents=... orphans=...`) is parsed positionally and is not a declared stable interface. The consuming gate handles this without a version check, and the exact rule matters: it exits UNESTABLISHED when the summary line is absent or unreadable, when it reports fewer than one scanned document, or when awiki exits a code other than 0/1. When the line parses but omits `orphans`/`islands` it does NOT automatically fail — awiki legitimately omits both on a fully clean run — so a pass there requires awiki's own `ok` verdict token AND corroborating `orphan_rate=0` / `largest_component_ratio=1`; a summary that disagrees with itself reports UNPROVEN. So a format change on a new version reports UNPROVEN rather than a false clean verdict, without a version number being consulted.

host_notes: awiki is a quality VALIDATION support binary: discovered and installed through this manifest, then consumed by the repo's own `docs-graph` quality lane (`scripts/gates/check_docs_graph.py`). Both `doctor_policy` and `version_expectation.policy` stay ADVISORY, and that is now a MEASURED decision rather than a placeholder. An earlier note here said to tighten both once a gate consumed awiki; that instruction was tested and is WRONG. Setting `doctor_policy: required` makes any machine without awiki a `blocking-install-needed` doctor failure (measured: exit 1), and a non-advisory version policy makes a maintainer who merely upgrades awiki a `blocking-failure`. Neither buys safety, because the risk they would guard is already handled at the point of CONSUMPTION: the docs-graph lane reports UNPROVEN, never a pass, when the binary is absent OR when the summary line does not parse. That fires on the actual breakage instead of on a version number, and it leaves an ordinary contributor machine working.

The repository invocation is `awiki lint -root docs -recursive`, run from the repo root. A captured run at 0.5.0 lives at `charness-artifacts/quality/fixtures/awiki-0.5.0-docs-lint.json` and is checked by `tools/check_quality_tool_fixtures.py`.

This manifest declares the binary and its lifecycle. It does NOT add an entry to `.agents/quality-adapter.yaml`, and it does not put awiki into the shipped CONSUMER quality contract — adoption stays opt-in through this manifest. The sentence that used to stand here said it does not make awiki a repo gate; that is no longer true and is corrected rather than left beside the note that supersedes it. charness's own `run-quality.sh` now runs a `docs-graph` lane over it, and the orphan disposition it once deferred to #518/#566 is done: `docs/index.md` links the graph and `orphans=0`.

awiki writes its help surface to STDERR, not stdout, and still exits 0 — so the healthcheck asserts `stderr_contains:Commands:`. A `stdout_contains:` criterion here reports a healthy binary as unhealthy; that was observed against 0.5.0, not assumed.

`detect` asserts `exit_code:0` only, diverging from siblings that add `stdout_contains:<tool>`. Observed, not assumed: `awiki --version` prints a bare `0.5.0` to stdout with no tool name, so a `stdout_contains:awiki` criterion would report a healthy binary as missing. The version string is still read from stdout, which is why `detected_by` is `stdout`.
